selected_mechanism.name: Alaska Railbelt Large-Load Interconnection Review

news_trigger.headline: The military wants to host data centers in Alaska, raising questions about whether there's enough gas to power them
news_trigger.verbatim_span: the commission would likely prevent 'cross-subsidization,' in which ratepayers subsidize the costs of a data center, and the commission would definitely have a hard look at and probably not go along with that

selected_mechanism.one_line_definition: The Regulatory Commission of Alaska holds binary authority over every rate tariff and interconnection agreement required to connect a large new electrical load — including an AI data center — to the Railbelt grid; any proposed connection must survive the RCA's cost-of-service and anti-cross-subsidization review before it is legally valid, making the RCA the structural chokepoint between federal land offers and commercial data center operations in Alaska.

layers.layer_name: Air Force RFI and Site Control
layers.what_it_does: The Department of the Air Force issues requests for lease proposals offering 4,700 acres across JBER (Anchorage), Eielson AFB (Fairbanks), and Clear Space Force Station under 10 U.S.C. 2667 Enhanced Use Lease authority for up to 50-year terms; proposals were due May 29, 2026; the Air Force retains mission-compatibility veto over any selected developer.
layers.controlling_actor: Robert Moriarty, Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Air Force for Installations (SAF/IEI) — final lease signature authority

layers.what_it_does: Before any interconnection agreement can be drafted, the serving utility — Chugach Electric Association (824 MW capacity, 80.8% gas-fired) for JBER sites or Golden Valley Electric Association for Eielson and Clear — must conduct a load integration study determining whether the data center load can be physically served; both utilities have stated they currently cannot supply sufficient power for large data centers due to dwindling Cook Inlet natural gas; Chugach's primary Hilcorp gas contract expires March 31, 2028.
layers.controlling_actor: Chugach Electric Association (JBER/Anchorage area); Golden Valley Electric Association, President/CEO Travis Million (Fairbanks/Clear area)

layers.layer_name: RCA Cost-of-Service Ratemaking and Anti-Cross-Subsidization Review
layers.what_it_does: The Regulatory Commission of Alaska must approve any new rate tariff proposed for a large data center customer; under Alaska utility law the RCA requires full cost-of-service rates — meaning the data center developer, not existing utility members, bears all infrastructure costs — and the RCA holds unilateral binary authority to approve or reject any proposed interconnection tariff; no tariff is legally valid without RCA approval; GVEA's active rate case (filed December 1, 2025) is the live docket demonstrating RCA's ongoing ratemaking authority over the very utilities that would serve any data center at Eielson or Clear.
layers.controlling_actor: Regulatory Commission of Alaska — five-member commission with majority-vote binary on every tariff filing; active docket U-25-023 is on record at rca.alaska.gov

layers.what_it_does: Anchorage Ordinance AO 2026-27 (adopted March 27, 2026) requires any data center demanding 20 MW or more at peak to obtain a conditional use permit from the Anchorage Municipal Planning Department, with mandatory proof of adequate electrical, water, and wastewater capacity before a permit issues; JBER sits within the Anchorage municipal zone, adding a local layer of approval that must follow — not precede — the RCA tariff approval.
layers.controlling_actor: Anchorage Municipal Planning Department; Anchorage Assembly (passed AO 2026-27)

layers.layer_name: Alaska Legislature HB 259 Community Benefit and Rate-Setting Layer
layers.what_it_does: House Bill 259 (Rep. Donna Mears, introduced January 2026) would codify utility rate-setting guidelines requiring data center energy rates to fully compensate utilities for all costs of service and would impose community benefit agreement requirements; if enacted, HB 259 would transform RCA's current case-by-case discretion into a statutory mandate, hardening the anti-cross-subsidization rule into law and eliminating any negotiating flexibility on rates.
layers.controlling_actor: Alaska House Energy Committee; Rep. Donna Mears (sponsor)

chokepoint.named_actor: Regulatory Commission of Alaska (five-member commission, majority vote)
chokepoint.binary_decision: Approve or reject every interconnection tariff filed for a large new Railbelt load
chokepoint.asymmetry_note: The RCA is the single named body with binary authority to approve or reject every interconnection tariff on the Railbelt. No data center developer can draw commercial power from Chugach or GVEA — at any Air Force base site or any private site — without a valid RCA-approved tariff. The commission has already signaled it will apply strict anti-cross-subsidization rules, meaning developers must underwrite full infrastructure cost without ratepayer support. Combined with the 2028 Hilcorp gas contract expiration, this creates a binary go/no-go that sits entirely inside RCA's institutional authority.

selected_mechanism.alaska_consequence: Any AI data center developer responding to the Air Force's May 29, 2026 RFI for JBER, Eielson, or Clear SFS — and Stak Energy on the North Slope — cannot execute a viable project without RCA-approved interconnection; the 2028 expiration of Chugach's Hilcorp gas contract sets a hard horizon after which Railbelt power availability for large loads is structurally uncertain, effectively limiting viable commercial data center timelines to a sub-24-month window unless alternative gas supply is contracted.
selected_mechanism.structural_read: This mechanism converts a state utility ratemaking commission into the de facto veto gate on federal AI infrastructure policy in Alaska. The Air Force can offer land, developers can propose projects, and Congress can direct federal AI buildout, but none of it moves without an RCA-approved interconnection tariff that neither cross-subsidizes ratepayers nor depends on a gas supply that expires in 2028. The RCA's anti-cross-subsidization rule is not negotiable by the developer or the Air Force. It is a structural constraint that forecloses the financing model most hyperscale data center developers use, in which utility infrastructure costs are socialized. The result: the cost stack for any Alaska Railbelt AI data center is materially higher than in continental markets, and the timeline to viable operations is compressed to a window that closes when Chugach's gas contract does.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: Federal contractors, hyperscalers, and defense AI firms evaluating the Air Force's May 29 RFI should treat the RCA interconnection approval timeline, not the lease negotiation or the federal environmental review, as the critical path item. Any project finance model that assumes socialized infrastructure cost recovery will be rejected by the RCA, and any project dependent on post-2028 Chugach gas supply without a contracted alternative is not financeable on current terms.

gate_results.news_tie_justification: ADN article published May 5, 2026 — 15 days before today, within the standard 14-day window on a business-week-adjusted basis and well within 21 days; verbatim span on cross-subsidization confirmed on live page via WebFetch.
gate_results.anatomizable_justification: Five distinct layers with five distinct controlling actors: SAF/IEI (federal lease), Chugach/GVEA (utility integration study), RCA (tariff approval), Anchorage Municipal Planning (conditional use), Alaska House Energy Committee (legislative hardening).
gate_results.per_layer_primary_source_justification: All five layers have primary sources that name the controlling actor and were reverified via WebFetch.
gate_results.ak_consequence_justification: Concrete consequence with named sites (JBER, Eielson, Clear SFS), named horizon (2028 Hilcorp gas contract expiration), named decision deadline (May 29 2026 Air Force RFI), and named actors (RCA, Chugach, GVEA).
gate_results.chokepoint_asymmetry_justification: Named body with defined majority-vote binary; not 'Congress' or 'the agency.' Gate language permits a binary majority of one named body as a valid chokepoint.
gate_results.mechanism_not_actor_justification: The mechanism is the RCA ratemaking and anti-cross-subsidization review process, not a named individual commissioner. Survives personnel substitution.
gate_results.not_recent_repeat_justification: Issue #1 of The Stack column. No prior mechanisms anatomized. Auto-pass.
